size.note: Newman's Yellow-billed Kite page (Milvus parasitus) gives 55 cm. Project slug is milvus-migrans with Afrikaans Swartwou; taxonomy note required.

habitat: Wide range of habitats; often aggregates at food sources. Common Kruger summer kite is the yellow-billed African form (Newman's; SABAP1).
summary: Fork-tailed scavenger kite. In Kruger the abundant summer bird is the Yellow-billed form (often split as M. aegyptius/parasitus): adult with yellow-based bill, brown head, dark eye, deeply forked tail. Palearctic Black Kite (M. m. migrans) is scarcer, with darker bill and paler head (Newman's; SABAP1).

similar.note: Booted Eagle pale morph can show a kite-like pale upperwing panel but lacks a forked tail (Newman's).

research.note: Research confidence was medium-high and is stored as medium. The list keeps Milvus migrans (Black Kite, Swartwou), matching the IOC name used in this repo. Newman's splits Yellow-billed Kite (Milvus parasitus, Geelbekwou). Kruger's common summer kite is the yellow-billed African form, and the structured marks are that form. The scarcer black-billed Palearctic bird is described in the summary. No seasonal plumage change is described in the sources consulted, except presence/absence of migrants. Gaps: No Kruger-labelled image in the selected set. Structured marks keep the common form. The black-kite form is not a separate variant. Palearctic Black Kite (M. m. migrans): blacker bill, pale greyish head, pale eyes, less deeply forked tail (Newman's comparison; SABAP1). Scarcer in southern Africa than Yellow-billed. The schema has no morph field. Colour phrases outside the vocabulary were stored as the nearest swatch: dark to dark-brown. Project lists a single milvus-migrans (Black Kite / Swartwou). Newman's and modern SA lists often split Yellow-billed Kite (Geelbekwou, M. parasitus/aegyptius) from Black Kite (Swartwou, M. migrans). SABAP1 treated Yellowbilled as M. m. parasitus and Black as M. m. migrans/lineatus on the same spread (126). Research record covers both forms and flags the split.
